name: h3-prompt-dictionary
description: Machine rules for H3 call text and dialogue rows. A gate reads this file and refuses or warns by name; the prompt-writing skill documents the same law in prose. One source of truth, two consumers.

waivers.law: A press may name a waiver (params.prompt_waivers: ["RULE-ID"]). The gate refuses by default; a named waiver passes the press and is recorded in the run receipt with the rule id and the message it overrode. Never add a waiver silently.

rules.message: call {index} has {words} words. H3 needs at least 90 (target 95-128): state style, scene + subject, pose/motion continuity, and camera + ambient sound. Under 90 the model invents the missing detail.
rules.cite: vendor examples 85/81/93 words at 5.2/8.0/6.0 s; estate conformance floor

rules.message: call {index} never states the medium. Open with one flat style line ('Live-action, cinematic, ...' / '2D-animated, flat cel shading, ...') and repeat it in every call of the film.
rules.cite: vendor §5 examples open with the medium

rules.message: call {index} has no camera move from the closed vocabulary. Use one of the vendor verbs (Push In, Pull Out, Pan Left/Right, Truck Left/Right, Tilt Up/Down, Pedestal Up/Down, Arc Shot, Tracking Shot, Static Shot, Shake Slightly/Strongly, POV, Roll Clockwise/Counterclockwise) with amplitude and speed.
call {index} says 'pan up/down'. A pan pivots horizontally; a vertical scan is 'Tilt Up/Down' or 'Pedestal Up/Down'. Write the vendor verb.
rules.cite: base-en.txt §4.3 (the list has no pan up)

rules.message: call {index} pastes vendor scaffolding or a shot header. The card composes those; a call stays ONE continuous action line with no [Shot n] header and no 'For the target video' lines.
rules.cite: card doc: the card composes the guide's scaffolding itself

rules.message: call {index} names speech without the vendor spoken form. Speakers are (S1)/(S2) and the words ride verbatim in <d>[English] ...</d>. Better: put the line in an audio_clips row and keep the call free of dialogue.

the film's call text describes speech but no audio_clips row carries it in that window. The words move the mouth only when placed as a row (text = exact words, start_frame, dur_frames). Prose does not move it.
rules.cite: card doc: the words move the mouth; measured round 37

rules.message: ref_audios is armed while dialogue rows are placed. Measured: the row's voice wins and the audio reference adds nothing (copy correlation 0.827/0.545 identical in both arms, RMS equal to 4 dp). Keep the reference only when the row's voice must be replaced; otherwise disarm it to avoid the last-window collage.

calls.text: A woman stands on a beach.

Live-action, cinematic, shallow depth of field. She stands on wet sand at dusk in a pale blue bikini, hair loose and salt drying on her shoulders, both feet planted with her weight on the left, the right knee soft, arms low and open away from her sides. The camera pushes in with small amplitude at slow speed toward her face, holding as the light comes through the spray. Beyond her the waterline keeps its slow rhythm. Breakers roll behind her, wind moves the loose strands, and wet sand gives slightly under the balls of her feet.
